1.pericope_label: Woe to her that is filthy and polluted, to the oppressing city!
debates: Which Jerusalem the woe is addressed to
Whose voice she refused to hear
What the word polluted alludes to
outliers: Gill dates the woe to the second temple and the coming of Christ rather than to the years before the captivity
Ellicott turns the two negatives into contrasts, wealth trusted instead of God and other gods drawn near instead of him
themes: Sin hated most in those nearest to God
Righteous statutes administered unrighteously
Washings that never reached the life
A city telling the Almighty to depart

3.pericope_label: Her princes within her are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves
debates: Whether they leave the bones for the morrow or leave nothing at all
Who the princes and prophets are
What the word rendered light means
outliers: Ellicott reverses the received sense of the clause about the bones, making the point their greed rather than their leavings
Calvin turns the passage into an argument that a faithful few may stand against numbers
themes: A comparison the Hebrew leaves unstated
Judges who work between evening and morning
Robbery practised in the court of justice
A title conceded to men who dishonour it

5.pericope_label: The just Lord is in the midst thereof; he will not do iniquity
debates: Whether the presence in the midst is a comfort or an aggravation
Whether the iniquity not done is God own or the people
What bringing judgment to light every morning describes
outliers: Gill refers the title of the just Lord to Christ and to his presence in the temple
Calvin makes the clause a concession quoted back from the mouths of those who pleaded it
themes: A presence that neither deterred nor allured
A boast granted and then turned around
A God who did not cease to be himself on moving in
Judgment brought to light with each morning

6.pericope_label: I have cut off the nations: their towers are desolate; I made their streets waste
debates: Which nations were cut off
Whether God speaks an expectation or an unfulfilled wish
What rising early to corrupt their doings describes
outliers: Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch both turn the opening of the seventh verse into a wish or entreaty rather than an expectation
Calvin argues from the comparative innocence of the nations that the warning ought to have told more, not less
themes: Neighbours punished as a warning to a spared people
A green tree reasoning about the dry
Cities described as hunted down
Diligence spent on finding room for sin

8.pericope_label: Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the Lord, until the day that I rise up to the prey
debates: Whether the command to wait is addressed to the faithful or to the incorrigible
What rising up to the prey means
How far all the earth extends
outliers: Calvin knowingly rejects the reading held by almost all, and makes the verse a dismissal rather than an invitation
Clarke narrows all the earth to the land of Judah where the others extend it to the whole world
themes: Grace taking its occasion from human badness
A verb that is only ever used of believing patience
A God who comes as a lion after sparing too long
Judgment that begins at the house of God

9.pericope_label: For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord
debates: Whose lip the pure language belongs to
Whether the dispersed are scattered Jews or Gentile nations
What the offering brought consists of
outliers: Ellicott alone makes the dispersed the Gentile tribes rather than the exiled people of Israel
Clarke takes pure language to mean a form of worship rather than speech at all
themes: A promise added so the faithful would not despair
The discord of Babel undone
Speech taken as the organ of the heart
Homage counted as a bloodless offering

11.pericope_label: In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me
debates: Whether the end of shame rests on pardon or on amended conduct
What the two words afflicted and poor describe
How absolutely the promise about not doing iniquity is meant
outliers: Calvin argues that the people had to be broken because they could not be bent
Ellicott finds a play between the word for afflicted and the word for meek
themes: Sin seen in the glass of pardoning love
Privileges turned into a pretext for obduracy
A tenth part offered as compensation for the rest
A people humbled and reduced together

14.pericope_label: Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart
debates: Why the summons to rejoice comes before the deliverance
Whether the judgments removed are outward or inward as well
Who the cast-out enemy is
outliers: Henry prefers a rendering that has the enemy swept out as dirt is swept to a dunghill
Wesley attaches a condition to the promise that they shall see evil no more
themes: Trouble removed once its cause is gone
Thanks demanded for a blessing still far off
Grievances left that are no longer judgments
A throne empty until one king takes it

16.pericope_label: In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem, Fear thou not: and to Zion, Let not thine hands be slack
debates: Who speaks the words of encouragement
What resting in his love means
Who the sorrowful gathered in the last verse are
outliers: Ellicott renders the clause as keeping silence in love and reads the pair as a bridegroom yearning and shouting
Calvin makes the word for time mean a determined season, and turns the verse into a rebuke of impatience
themes: Congratulation offered from every side at once
Hands that fear has emptied of strength
Quiet given for duty and not for torpor
A season fixed by the giver and not the asker

19.pericope_label: Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee: and I will save her that halteth
debates: What the opening verb means when its object is left unstated
Who is meant by her that halteth
Why the word for captivity stands in the plural
outliers: Calvin blames interpreters who reduce the plural captivities to one, since the people were many troops of captives rather than one
Clarke reports a rendering in which God works with the people for their sake rather than dealing with their oppressors
themes: A verb left without its object
A maimed sheep carried back with the flock
Slow deliverance offered as a reason not to despair
Witnesses promised a sight they cannot imagine
